messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a ~3x provisional charge spike for a handful of streaming sessions right after the router circuit-breaker tripped during yesterday's canary. Looks tied to midstream reconnects + toolcall retries + truncation.
sam: ugh. any obvious dup keys or missing idempotency? :thinking_face:
anya: Not obvious. Router logs show a flurry of reconnects and early EOFs. Tool service responded with 502 for some chunks so client retried. Billing shows provisional tokens for both original and retry traces.
kevin: paste of router excerpt below — timestamps truncated for thread:
```
[2023-12-12T21:04:12Z] session=abc123 route=canary cb=tripped reason=socket_eof
[2023-12-12T21:04:12Z] session=abc123 reconnect attempt=1 origin=proxy-2
[2023-12-12T21:04:13Z] toolcall id=tool-xyz status=502 chunk=1/5
[2023-12-12T21:04:14Z] client retry new_session=def456 orig_session=abc123
[2023-12-12T21:04:15Z] billing provisional tokens session=def456 tokens=120
[2023-12-12T21:04:15Z] billing provisional tokens session=abc123 tokens=90
```
matt: So provisional tokens are being issued per session id and when we reconnect we create a new session id and both get credited. That matches prior issues but we expected reconciler to merge on orig_session metadata.
anya: Right — reconciler needs an "orig_session" link to avoid double-crediting, but router doesn't always set it during a circuit-breaker handoff (we create fresh sessions to prioritize latency). That break in provenance is the root cause.
sam: Two angles: 1) minimum: make reconciler merge on parent trace id if present. 2) longer: mutate router to attach session_origin header on reconnects so billing has stable identity (even for ephemeral handoffs).
kevin: For 1) reconciler merging could cause false merges if sessions legitimately overlap (e.g., dual requests). We should only auto-merge when there's a clear parent link (orig_session) or same client request id.
anya: Agreed. Proposal: change router to always forward X-Session-Origin: <orig_session|empty> on reconnects. Add a safety check in reconciler: only dedupe provisional tokens when origin header exists AND delta < 30s.
matt: UX/Console impact: the billing console currently shows two separate provisional lines and customers raise support tickets. If we dedupe later we must surface a notice: "Provisional charges merged due to routing handoff" in cost timeline.
billing-bot: FYI — current refund policy allows auto-refund for duplicated provisional tokens if reconciler flags duplicate within 24h. We need a signal from reconciler to trigger auto-refund flow (API: POST /internal/billing/resolve?id=<merge_id>).@kevin can you wire that?
kevin: I'll add a merge_id to reconciler output. Quick question: do we need a rollout guard? Changing router header could affect older Dedicated clusters.
anya: Yes — add a feature flag on router: feature.attach_session_origin. Rollout plan: enable in canary region -> 1% -> 25% -> 100% over 48h. Monitor dedupe_rate and any increase in 502 footguns.
sam: Telemetry: add counters: router.session_origin_sent, reconciler.merged_provisional_count, reconciliation.merge_latency. Dashboards in Console: show merged_provisional as separate line in cost breakdown and a toggle to show pre-merge items.
matt: Also add a small note in rollouts UI: "This flag changes session provenance for reconnects; enabling may reduce duplicate provisional charges but could change session trace topology." Short doc blurb for SREs.
kevin: Implementation plan: patch router (2 files), reconciler (add merge_id + heuristics), billing webhook (accept merge_id). I'll open PRs. ETA: 2 days for router + reconciler; billing hook depends on reviews.
anya: Tests needed: unit for orig_session header preservation, integration test simulating midstream cb and toolcall 502 triggering retry + reconcilation, e2e verifying merged provisional shows in console with note.
matt: +1. Also add a metric that counts instances where reconciler refused to merge due to no origin header — helps us estimate how much of the problem we'll fix by header alone.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: router-canary-v3 -> canary-region -> 2023-12-13T04:00Z. /deploy router-canary-v3
anya: Thanks. I'll follow the canary and monitor reconciler merged_provisional_count and customer tickets for spike. If anything odd, roll back and we iterate on heuristics.
sam: If you see large refunds triggering, ping finance too so they don't auto-escalate.
billing-bot: Noted. Will throttle auto-refunds to 10/min for first 2h of rollout to avoid flash refunds.
anya: Cool. I'll open a short ops runbook snippet and link here when done.
sam: Thanks all :thumbsup:"
